about: The layout explorer's own tree — every layout on the site, one branch per family, with the real page (or the layout standard's own wire drawing) each id points at. Adding a layout is one object here; see readme.md.
title: Explorer

children.title: One column
children.description: The only questions are how wide it may get, and whether its height is divided instead.

children.title: Two columns
children.description: One decision: is the room shared evenly, or does one column support the other?

children.title: Sidebar
children.description: A narrow column beside a wide one. Five real pages below try different tops for the rail, and one asks who should own it.

children.title: Three columns
children.description: Where a layout gets a middle. Which side the narrow columns sit on is the whole difference.

children.title: Many
children.description: The count is not fixed, or is only fixed because a footer really means it.

children.title: Mobile
children.description: Real pages built to still work at 400 pixels wide.

children.title: Mega
children.description: Real pages built to spend a 3440 ultrawide screen on purpose.

children.title: How to choose
children.description: Five questions, asked in order, with live demos of a fit and a miss.

children.title: The approved five
children.description: A closed set with floors and ceilings at every level — the contract that keeps a new page from inventing a sixth.
